hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? what pulls at your attention most on an ordinary day?
options: same for most people. today, a word for one center.
real things. today, a word that puts them in their place.
then today’s word is made for you. listen.

steps.line: In Mecca’s early years, a man named Bilal was enslaved. He had become a Muslim, and the man who owned him wanted him to take it back.
The early biographies say he was made to lie on the hot sand at noon, with a heavy rock placed on his chest. “Give it up,” they told him.

steps.q: Bilal won’t take it back, day after day. Who do you think finally ends his torture?
o: His owner, who tires of it and lets him go
Abu Bakr, who buys him and sets him free
The Prophet ﷺ, who pays the ransom himself
steps.why: Abu Bakr, the Prophet’s ﷺ closest friend and a merchant, bought him. The early biographies say he freed several enslaved believers who were being punished for their faith.

steps.line: He said only one word, again and again. “Ahad. Ahad.” One. One. Later, Abu Bakr, a friend of the Prophet ﷺ, bought him and set him free.

steps.q: They wanted him to give up his faith. Why might one word have been enough?
o: It was easier to say through the pain
It said his whole faith at once
It was all the Arabic prayer he knew
steps.why: They wanted him to praise their idols. “One” refused them and affirmed God in a single breath.

steps.line: His word sits inside the prayer too. After four lines about God, al-Fatiha turns and speaks to Him: “You alone we worship, You alone we ask for help.”

steps.q: Al-Fatiha is recited in every unit of the five daily prayers. How many times a day is that, at least?
o: Five times, once in each prayer
steps.why: Fajr has two units, Maghrib three, the other three prayers four each: seventeen. So “You alone” is said at least seventeen times a day.

steps.line: In the Arabic, “You” comes first: iyyaka na‘budu, You we worship. Putting it first means only You. The word for that is tawhid, making one.

steps.q: Years later, in Medina, Bilal was given a famous job. What was it?
o: The first to give the call to prayer
The first judge of the city
Keeper of the keys of the Kaaba
steps.why: Bilal became the first muezzin. The voice that said “One” under the rock now called the city to prayer.

steps.line: Today, a phone buzzes, the inbox fills, a worry tugs. Tawhid says all of it is real, and none of it is God. One center, instead of a dozen.
steps.label: today

say: here’s what i love. they could put a rock on bilal’s chest, but they couldn’t move his center. one word held it.
in islam, tawhid is the heart of everything: God is one, with no partner. al-fatiha says it to God directly, “You alone,” in every prayer.

steps.q: Bilal’s one word and al-Fatiha’s “You alone” say the same thing. Under the rock, what was that word telling his owner?
o: “You may own me, but not my worship”
steps.why: Tawhid in one breath: no owner, no pain, no fear gets the place that belongs to God. That’s why it enraged the men standing over him.

today.say: today, try one small tawhid moment. when something tugs hard at you, a deadline, a worry, a screen, say quietly: “real, but not God.” if you pray, you can rest one word there, as bilal did: ahad.
options: that’s plenty. bilal began with one word too.

card.keepWhy: One center, instead of a dozen.
sources: Ibn Hisham, Sirat Rasul Allah (from Ibn Ishaq): Umayya ibn Khalaf laid Bilal on the sand of the valley at the noon heat with a great rock on his chest; Bilal said “ahad, ahad”; Abu Bakr bought and freed him
Sunan Ibn Majah 150 (Ibn Mas‘ud: the first to show their Islam were seven, among them Bilal, who kept saying “ahad, ahad”; graded hasan)
Qur’an 1:5 (“Thee (alone) we worship; Thee (alone) we ask for help,” Pickthall)
Qur’an 112:1 (“Say: He is Allah, the One!”)
The fronted object iyyaka gives exclusivity (only You): e.g. Ibn Kathir on 1:5
check: The rock on the chest is from the sira (Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham), not from Ibn Majah 150, which has the sun and “ahad, ahad”. Confirm the sira wording is fine to tell.
